remediation.suggestion: Label examples as illustrative and keep unsafe examples under clear warning headings.

content.user_title: Apply Architecture Patterns for Next.js Teams
content.value_statement: Teams often lose time choosing patterns for features. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a concise architecture guide for consistent implementation.
actual_capabilities: Maps architecture decisions to server components, client components, route handlers, and server actions.
Summarizes strict TypeScript conventions for types, guards, assertions, and return annotations.
Documents Drizzle ORM queries, relations, transactions, migrations, and SQL injection prevention.
Explains API route structure with Zod validation, authentication, authorization, and consistent responses.
Compares state management choices across React Query, useState, Context, URL state, and form state.
Highlights React 19 patterns such as use, useOptimistic, useFormStatus, and useActionState.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not an executable analyzer or code generator.
It links to related local skills that may be unavailable outside the original repository.
Examples use simplified names and imports that must be adapted to each project.
It does not verify live framework documentation or project-specific constraints.

use_cases.title: Choose a Feature Architecture
use_cases.description: Plan whether a feature should use a server component, client component, server action, or API route.

use_cases.title: Review Implementation Consistency
use_cases.description: Compare code against TypeScript, API, database, and state management conventions before merging.

use_cases.title: Onboard Project Contributors
use_cases.description: Teach established framework patterns with quick references, decision trees, and examples.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Component Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: I need to display project data and add a delete button. Use the architecture patterns to choose server and client boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Design an API Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a create project endpoint using the API patterns. Include validation, auth checks, ownership checks, status codes, and response shape.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor State Choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature state usage against the state patterns. Recommend React Query, useState, Context, URL state, or form state.

prompt_templates.title: Run an Architecture Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned feature across Next.js, TypeScript, Drizzle, API, React 19, and state patterns. Identify tradeoffs and follow-up skills.

output_examples.input: I need to add a project dashboard with filters and creation forms.
output: Use a server component for initial dashboard data.
Use URL state for filters that need shareable links.
Use a server action for simple creation.
Use React Query only when client refetching is required.

output_examples.input: Review an API route design for creating users.
output: Define a Zod schema before reading trusted fields.
Return clear status codes and consistent errors.

output_examples.input: Help a new contributor understand the project patterns.
output_examples.output: Start with the decision trees, then read the focused pattern file for the selected area. Use the linked specialized skill for implementation details.

best_practices: Start with the decision trees, then read the linked pattern file for the chosen area.
Keep server data on the server unless client interaction requires a client component.
Validate API input and check authorization before running business logic.
anti_patterns: Using Context or useState for server data that needs caching and refetching.
Copying examples without adapting imports, schemas, auth helpers, and database tables.
Skipping linked specialized skills when a feature needs detailed implementation guidance.

faq.question: Does this skill execute code?
faq.answer: No. It is documentation that guides architecture choices and examples.

faq.question: Which stack does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Next.js, React 19, TypeScript, Drizzle ORM, Zod, and React Query.

faq.question: Can it replace specialized skills?
faq.answer: No. It points to specialized skills when detailed implementation guidance is needed.

faq.question: Is it useful for code review?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to compare feature code against documented architecture and type safety patterns.

faq.question: Does it include security guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers validation, authentication, authorization, and SQL injection prevention at a pattern level.

faq.question: Can it update my project automatically?
faq.answer: No. Claude, Codex, or Claude Code must still apply changes using your normal tools and approvals.
